regnum

A ruler's reign, from accession to end, and the territory they held when it ended. Who was it?
Hints · no penalty, but your share card counts how many you opened
Historical borders: historical-basemaps by André Ourednik and contributors (GPL-3.0), using the snapshot nearest each reign's end and smoothed. Approximate.
Coastlines: Natural Earth (public domain), via world-atlas.
Game format inspired by Lifelines. Regnum is an independent fan project with no affiliation.

How to play

The shaded area is a kingdom or empire as it stood when one ruler's reign ended. The two years in the corner are when that reign began and ended. Your job is to name the ruler. You get three guesses.

If you guess wrong, you'll see how many years apart the two reigns were. Your guess also appears on the map, with its own territory outlined and its capital marked, so you can see how close you were.

Stuck? There are three hints: a bit of trivia, the capital and the dynasty. Opening the capital also tells you how far, and in which direction, each of your guesses was from the right capital. Opening the dynasty tells you whether any of your guesses belonged to the same one. Hints don't cost you anything, but your shared result shows how many you used.

Use Close-up and World to zoom in and out. There's a new ruler every day, and Practice gives you as many extra rounds as you like.

Sources

Historical borders come from historical-basemaps by André Ourednik and contributors (GPL-3.0). Each map uses the snapshot closest to the end of the reign, so treat the borders as approximate. Coastlines are from Natural Earth (public domain), via world-atlas. Some reign dates are disputed by historians, so a few are approximate. The game was inspired by Lifelines, and it isn't affiliated with it.
